Subject: Seniority adjudication: L5 vs L6 engineering lead (matrix review)

Irene / team —

Quick ask: we have an advanced candidate (Oliver Grant) for the ML Infrastructure Lead opening on the Core Serving team. Summary: strong background in distributed systems for inference, led infra initiatives at previous employer that reduced tail latency by 28%, ~9 years total experience, recent IC lead owning cross-team infra standards. Hiring manager wants an expedited offer but there is uncertainty whether this should be anchored as L5 (senior IC) or L6 (staff-equivalent).

Attached: comp_band_matrix_May2026.xlsx and Oliver's resume. Proposed comp anchors in the doc (base / target eq / signing) reflect an L5 top-of-band and an L6 midpoint.

Questions for calibration:
- Does the committee feel Oliver's scope warrants L6 (staff) versus L5 with a growth plan?
- If L6, we need signoff from compensation and Marissa for budget + HC delta.
- If L5, can we include a 6–9 month success milestone tied to an L6 re-eval?

Relevant context: role is individual contributor with heavy cross-team coordination; no direct people management expected initially. Hiring manager flagged potential to be a technical lead across product and infra.

Can you weigh in with which anchor and whether we should proceed with the L5-stretch offer or escalate to L6 approval?

Thanks —
Karthik
Talent Partner | Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifying items before I weigh in formally:
- Did Oliver have direct ownership of architecture (not just performance wins) that affected multiple product lines?
- Any evidence of influence on roadmap or headcount decisions at his prior org?
- Is the hiring manager prepared to accept potential scope mismatch if we anchor L5 today?

Operational note: we prefer to avoid offering L6 unless the candidate demonstrates demonstrable cross-organizational impact and a pattern of shaping other teams' technical direction. If it's borderline, an L5 offer with an explicit 6-9 month success plan (milestones and quant metrics) is our usual lever.

If you can add a brief bullet list of the candidate's cross-team deliverables, I can provide a firm recommendation to comp.

– Irene
Irene Choi

On Mon, May 11, 2026 at 11:05 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> If it's borderline, an L5 offer with an explicit 6-9 month success plan (milestones and quant metrics) is our usual lever.

Karthik / Irene —

I've reviewed Oliver's resume and the comp matrix. My read: technically strong and experienced owning infra projects end-to-end, but I don't see a sustained pattern of org-level influence or multiple teams attributing roadmap changes to him. That said, he has one large program where he was the de facto standards owner for a team of 8.

Recommendation: extend an L5 (senior IC) offer at top-of-band with a documented success plan that includes:
- measurable latency/reliability targets for Q3
- ownership of a cross-team API/standards piece within 6 months
- a technical review and ramp checkpoint at month 6 for re-eval towards L6 if milestones met

If Marissa is comfortable with this growth path, comp can approve L5-top-of-band without escalating to the comp committee.

Jonas
VP, Core Serving Engineering

TL;DR — I will approve L6 only if the candidate shows: (1) multiple examples of cross-org technical direction, (2) measurable product-level outcomes tied to their decisions, and (3) evidence of mentoring/senior influence beyond immediate peers.

In Oliver's case, the resume shows high individual impact but limited evidence of consistent cross-org leadership. I'm okay moving forward with an L5-top-of-band offer provided we:
- make the growth plan explicit in the offer (6-month checkpoints)
- include an accelerated review clause that schedules a formal re-eval at month 6 with engineering leadership
- reserve a modest signing bonus to make the package competitive without breaking HC for an L6 anchor

If Karthik confirms the hiring manager accepts those terms, Marissa signs off.

Marissa Cole
Head of Engineering Operations | Redwood Inference
